description: Check that converted amounts follow from the rates supplied. The converted figure is the exact product rounded once to the target currency minor unit under the stated mode, and a difference is reported with its exact size, because one unit is a rounding choice and a thousand is a wrong rate. Also reports two rates for one pair on one date, which means two sources. Pay 160000 atomic USDC on Base via exact x402. MCP does not pay; it provides a challenge handoff.

conversions.description: The conversions to check. Nothing is fetched and no system is connected, so the data supplied is the whole input.

from_amount.description: The amount converted. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

on.description: The rate date, which is what makes two rates for one pair comparable. A calendar date as YYYY-MM-DD.

rate.description: Target units per source unit. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

to_amount.description: The amount produced. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

minor_units.description: Decimal places per currency code, overriding the published table. Two is the default because most currencies have two.

require_one_rate_per_pair.description: Report two rates for one pair on one date. Defaults to true.

rounding.description: How a figure is rounded. Required rather than defaulted in spirit: half-up and half-even disagree on every price ending in 5, so the mode is an accounting policy and is published in the response. Defaults to half_up when omitted.

name: fx_conversion_consistency_audit

complete.description: Whether everything supplied was examined. False means part of it was not, which is a different problem from something that is wrong.

consistent.description: True only when every conversion followed from its rate and every rate was consistent across its pair.

finding_count.description: The true total, even when the listing is bounded.

passed.description: The same verdict under the name shared across the caller-supplied families.

request_id.description: Delivery request identifier; also returned in x-foundry-request-id.

title: FX Conversion Consistency Audit
